newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says ASEAN to convey ideas to Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says ASEAN to convey ideas to Hun Sen.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Friday the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) would offer ideas to Cambodian strongman Hun Sen on ways to resolve the political crisis in his nation.

"Tomorrow, I will go to Phnom Penh where three ASEAN foreign ministers will meet Prime Minister Hun Sen. The three ASEAN foreign ministers will convey ideas on how we can contribute to a settlement of the Cambodia crisis," Alatas told reporters.
Alatas and foreign ministers Prachuab Chaiyasan of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines will arrive in Phnom Pehn on Saturday.
An aide to Hun Sen said the three foreign ministers will meet with him.
Alatas declined to give details of the proposals to be made.
"It is difficult to say at this stage. We want to see how to restore political stability in Cambodia," he said.

Cambodia was scheduled to join ASEAN in late July, but the grouping postponed Cambodia's membership indefinitely in response to Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of his senior coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
ASEAN currently comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Alatas said ASEAN had held talks with King Sihanouk and Ranariddh. "I have been given indications that both leaders have showed their acceptance of the ASEAN proposals," Alatas said.
He said if there was a positive response from Hun Sen, the ASEAN team may meet Ranariddh and Sihanouk again.
